server.instructions:
CandleStack is a lab for experiments on financial time series: a user uploads a trading model (Keras or ONNX), describes its input in a manifest and backtests it on market data, crypto from Binance and US stocks from Alpaca, then compares the results and publishes the good ones.

You act as the user whose API key signed in. The key's scopes decide which tools work: read (everything that only reads), backtests, models and publish. Call get_me first to see who you act for and what the key may do. A tool that changes data says so in its annotations.

A failed tool call answers a problem as JSON: its type (https://candlestack.tech/problems/<slug>) names what went wrong and its detail says what to do.

Docs for agents: https://candlestack.tech/docs/agents/ and for this server: https://candlestack.tech/docs/mcp/. The resource candlestack://docs lists every docs page and reference.

backtests; `models`: upload models, add their manifests, rename, star and delete them;

methods and signing out need the browser session whatever the scopes.

tools.title: Get a model's manifest

tools.description:
Checks a manifest for one of the user's models without keeping it: a dry run of set_manifest, which changes nothing. It runs every check set_manifest runs: the form, the catalog (every block exists and sits in its step), the blocks' parameters, the names of the columns, the signature against the window and the columns, the shapes of the example, and the signature against the input and output read from the model file.

`valid` says whether every check passed. Else each of `problems` (at most 10; `more_problems` counts the rest) names its `field` (a path such as input.features[2].id), says what is wrong in `detail` and, when the check knows them, lists the values that fit there in `allowed`: fix those fields and check again, then call set_manifest.

Docs: https://candlestack.tech/docs/mcp/tools/#validate_manifest

manifest.description: The manifest as a JSON object, version 1: `version`, `input` (timeframe, session, representation, features with their normalization, window), `signature` (input and output shapes) and optionally `example` and `about`. Guide: https://candlestack.tech/docs/manifest; JSON Schema: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/candlestack-tech/candlestack/main/docs/manifest.schema.json. At most 1 MB as JSON.

tools.title: Check a manifest

tools.description:
Gives one of the user's models its manifest, or replaces the one it has, when every check passes (the checks of validate_manifest); the model is then `ready` and can be backtested. A manifest that fails answers the problem manifest-check-failed, whose `problems` name the `field`, the `detail` and the `allowed` values of each thing wrong: fix them and call it again, or try a manifest with validate_manifest first.

The whole manifest is replaced: what you leave out is gone, the example included. A trial run of the model with the manifest follows in the background: get_model shows it `verified` when the model gave the output of the manifest's example, or `check_error` when it failed.

Docs: https://candlestack.tech/docs/mcp/tools/#set_manifest

tools.title: Delete a model

tools.description:
Makes a one-time link to upload a model file (Keras `.keras` or ONNX `.onnx`, at most 50 MB) into the user's models. You never send the file through a tool: the file goes from the user's computer to the link, either by running `command` (curl) in the folder the file is in, or by opening `page_url` in the browser and dropping the file there.

The link takes one file within 15 minutes and counts against the user's storage; the file is checked as any upload (a real model with trained weights, nothing from it run). Treat `url` and `command` like a key until the upload is done. Then call get_model_upload with the link's `id` to see how it went and get the new model's ID; give the model a manifest with set_manifest before backtesting it.

Docs: https://candlestack.tech/docs/mcp/tools/#create_model_upload
